data.title: Check Point Response to CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619, CVE-2026-115560 - PHP vulnerabilities may allow Remote Code Execution through Firewall web interfaces
symptoms:
• Under certain circumstances, PHP vulnerabilities may allow Remote Code Execution through firewall web interfaces.

  • These issues received the IDs CVE-2026-109618 (CVSS: 9.2) and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS: 9.2).
    Check Point products are not vulnerable to CVE-2026-115560.

  • Affected Products:

    Check Point Force Firewalls, Check Point Spark Firewalls, and Cloud Firewalls that use one or more of these features:

    • Mobile Access Portal (not applicable to Spark Firewalls)
    • Remote Access VPN with SSL Network Extender (not applicable to Spark Firewalls)
    • Remote Access VPN with SAML Realm authentication enabled
    • Identity Awareness Captive Portal enabled
    • UserCheck Portal
    • Zero Phishing

  • Affected Versions:

    • R81.20, R82, R82.10, R82.20
    • R80, R80.10, R80.20, R80.30, R80.40, R81, R81.10 (all EoS)
    • Spark Firewalls R81.10.x, R82.00.x
    • Spark Firewalls R77.20.x, R80.20.x (all EoS)

Not affected:

  • Check Point Portal and SaaS services are already patched against these vulnerabilities.
  • Check Point Security Management and Log Servers are not impacted by these vulnerabilities.
  • Maestro Orchestrator


Mitigation

Important Notes:

  • October, 23, 2026 at 18:30 GMT update: Check Point provided a Hotfix for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. See the Solution section.

  • Check Point Firewalls R82.20 protect themselves through the Check Point IPS signatures "PHP Remote Code Execution" even when IPS is not enabled and HTTPS Inspection is not active on these Check Point Firewalls.


(1) Mitigation procedure for Check Point Firewalls (including VSNext / Traditional VSX modes)

Show / Hide this section

Follow one of the available edit options below.

Note - In ClusterXL, you must perform the steps below on each ClusterXL Member.

Option 1 - Use the Vi editor:

  1. Connect to the command line on the Check Point Firewall.

  2. Log in to the Expert mode.

  3. If this Check Point Firewall is configured in the VSNext / Traditional VSX mode, go to the context with ID 0:

    vsenv 0

  4. Back up the current file:

    cp -v $CPDIR/web/Apache/conf/cp-httpd.conf{,_BKP}

  5. Edit the current file:

    vi $CPDIR/web/Apache/conf/cp-httpd.conf

  6. Add these lines at the end of the file:

    <If "req('Content-Type') =~ /multipart/i">
        Require all denied
    </If>

    Important: Make sure that this "<If>...</If>" block appears only one time in the cp-httpd.conf file.

  7. Save the changes in the file and exit Vi editor.

  8. Restart the relevant services.

    Run the commands in the order listed:

    • On Check Point Firewalls R82.20:

      mpclient stop-managed-portals

      mpclient start-managed-portals

    • On Check Point Firewalls R82.10 and R82:

      mpclient stopallportals

      mpclient startall

    • On Check Point Firewalls R81.20:

      mpclient list | /usr/bin/xargs -I{} /usr/bin/sh -c 'mpclient status {} | /usr/bin/grep -q "Portal is running" && (mpclient restart {} | grep -q "Portal restarted" || echo "Failed to handle the portal {}" )' ; echo "Done"

Option 2 - Use one pipeline of CLI commands:

  1. Connect to the command line on the Check Point Firewall.

  2. Log in to the Expert mode.

  3. Back up the current file:

    cp -v $CPDIR/web/Apache/conf/cp-httpd.conf{,_BKP}

  4. Run this pipeline of CLI commands:

    Important: Make sure that after running these commands, this "<If "req('Content-Type') =~ /multipart/i">...</If> block appears only one time in the cp-httpd.conf file.

    • On Check Point Firewalls R82.20:

      printf '\n%s\n%s\n%s\n' $'<If "req(\'Content-Type\') =~ /multipart/i">' ' Require all denied' '</If>' >> $CPDIR/web/Apache/conf/cp-httpd.conf ; mpclient stop-managed-portals ; mpclient start-managed-portals

    • On Check Point Firewalls R82.10 and R82:

      printf '\n%s\n%s\n%s\n' $'<If "req(\'Content-Type\') =~ /multipart/i">' ' Require all denied' '</If>' >> $CPDIR/web/Apache/conf/cp-httpd.conf ; mpclient stopallportals ; mpclient startall

    • On Check Point Firewalls R81.20:

      printf '\n%s\n%s\n%s\n' $'<If "req(\'Content-Type\') =~ /multipart/i">' ' Require all denied' '</If>' >> $CPDIR/web/Apache/conf/cp-httpd.conf ; mpclient list | /usr/bin/xargs -I{} /usr/bin/sh -c 'mpclient status {} | /usr/bin/grep -q "Portal is running" && (mpclient restart {} | grep -q "Portal restarted" || echo "Failed to handle the portal {}" )' ; echo "Done"


(2) Mitigation procedure for Maestro and ElasticXL (including VSNext / Traditional VSX modes)

Show / Hide this section

Option 1 - Use the Vi editor:

  1. Connect to the command line on the Security Group.

  2. Log in to the Expert mode.

  3. If this Security Group is configured in the VSNext / Traditional VSX mode, go to the context with ID 0:

    g_all vsenv 0

  4. Back up the current file:

    g_all cp -v $CPDIR/web/Apache/conf/cp-httpd.conf{,_BKP}

  5. Edit the current file:

    vi $CPDIR/web/Apache/conf/cp-httpd.conf

  6. Add these lines at the end of the file:

    <If "req('Content-Type') =~ /multipart/i">
        Require all denied
    </If>

    Important: Make sure that this "<If>...</If>" block appears only one time in the cp-httpd.conf file.

  7. Save the changes in the file and exit Vi editor.

  8. Copy the modified file to all Security Group Members:

    asg_cp2blades $CPDIR/web/Apache/conf/cp-httpd.conf

  9. Restart the relevant services.

    Run the commands in the order listed:

    • On Security Groups R82.20:

      g_all mpclient stop-managed-portals

      g_all mpclient start-managed-portals

    • On Security Groups R82.10 and R82:

      g_all mpclient stopallportals

      g_all mpclient startall

    • On Security Groups R81.20:

      g_all mpclient list | /usr/bin/xargs -I{} /usr/bin/sh -c 'mpclient status {} | /usr/bin/grep -q "Portal is running" && (mpclient restart {} | grep -q "Portal restarted" || echo "Failed to handle the portal {}" )' ; echo "Done"

Option 2 - Use one pipeline of CLI commands:

  1. Connect to the command line on the Security Group.

  2. Log in to the Expert mode.

  3. Back up the current file:

    g_all cp -v $CPDIR/web/Apache/conf/cp-httpd.conf{,_BKP}

  4. Run this pipeline of CLI commands:

    Important: Make sure that after running these commands, this "<If "req('Content-Type') =~ /multipart/i">...</If>" block appears only one time in the cp-httpd.conf file.

    • On Security Groups R82.20:

      g_all printf '\n%s\n%s\n%s\n' $'<If "req(\'Content-Type\') =~ /multipart/i">' ' Require all denied' '</If>' >> $CPDIR/web/Apache/conf/cp-httpd.conf ; g_all mpclient stop-managed-portals ; g_all mpclient start-managed-portals

    • On Security Groups R82.10 and R82:

      g_all printf '\n%s\n%s\n%s\n' $'<If "req(\'Content-Type\') =~ /multipart/i">' ' Require all denied' '</If>' >> $CPDIR/web/Apache/conf/cp-httpd.conf ; g_all mpclient stopallportals ; g_all mpclient startall

    • On Security Groups R81.20:

      g_all printf '\n%s\n%s\n%s\n' $'<If "req(\'Content-Type\') =~ /multipart/i">' ' Require all denied' '</If>' >> $CPDIR/web/Apache/conf/cp-httpd.conf ; g_all mpclient list | /usr/bin/xargs -I{} /usr/bin/sh -c 'mpclient status {} | /usr/bin/grep -q "Portal is running" && (mpclient restart {} | grep -q "Portal restarted" || echo "Failed to handle the portal {}" )' ; echo "Done"


(3) Mitigation procedure for Check Point Spark Firewalls

Show / Hide this section

Use one pipeline of CLI commands:

  1. Connect to the command line on the Check Point Spark Firewall.

  2. Log in to the Expert mode.

  3. Back up the current file:

    cp -v $CPDIR/conf/cp-httpd.conf{,_BKP}

  4. Run this pipeline of CLI commands:

    Important: Make sure that after running these commands, this "<If "req('Content-Type') =~ /multipart/i">...</If>" block appears only one time in the cp-httpd.conf file.

    printf '\n%s\n%s\n%s\n' $'<If "req(\'Content-Type\') =~ /multipart/i">' '    Require all denied' '</If>' >> $CPDIR/conf/cp-httpd.conf ; sfwd_stop ; sleep 3s ; sfwd_start
data.solution:
This problem was fixed. Download the Hotfix from the table below.

Important:

  • This Hotfix implements the PHP 7.4 published fix for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619.
  • This Hotfix is compatible with all Jumbo Hotfix Accumulator Takes.
  • This Hotfix should be installed on each Security Gateway / Cluster member / Security Group Member / Standalone server.
  • This Hotfix requires a reboot.

Recommended steps to deploy this fix after manual mitigation:

  1. Manually edit the $CPDIR/web/Apache/conf/cp-httpd.conf file and delete the added lines to remove the mitigation.
  2. Install the relevant Hotfix package from the tables below.
  3. Reboot your appliance.


    For Security Gateway / Cluster Members / Security Group Members / Standalone

    Notes:

    • October 26, 2026 8:40 GMT: Updated R82, R82.10, and R82.20 Hotfix packages to support installation on Standalone deployments (Firewall and Security Management installed on the same appliance). If you have already deployed the previous fix, no update is required.

    • October 28, 2026 11:50 GMT: Updated the R81.20 Hotfix package to address a problem with Mobile Access. This Hotfix must be installed on top of the Jumbo Hotfix Accumulator Take 166 or higher. If you use the Mobile Access Portal, you must install this Hotfix. If you do not use the Mobile Access Portal, you do not need to update the previously installed Hotfix.
